feed.title: Adden Lab
feed.subtitle: The Adden lab is interested in the evolution and neural basis of behaviour, particularly maternal care behaviours. We study tsetse flies to understand how sensory and neural systems change to support changing behavioural demands in both mothers and offspring.

entry.title: Job alert
entry.content:
We are recruiting two PhD students! Join us to study the olfactory ecology and behaviours of tsetse larvae, deadline December 2nd) or the evolution of maternal care behaviours in flies (deadline December 13th).

Questions? Get in touch!

entry.title: October news
entry.content: Andrea was a panelist at the Royal Society of Edinburgh’s Global Health workshop, where she joined Liz Bandason (Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources), Kit Longden (University of Cambridge), Douglas Armstrong and David Price (University of Edinburgh) to discuss “Small brains, big threats: Connectomics and the insects shaping global health”. The workshop was a wonderful opportunity to hear from and engage with experts from all over the world, including clinicians, educators and researchers. Check out the RSE’s write-up of the day here.
